## File: `references/languages/java.md`

### Detection signals — Java (Security: Identity & Access)

Detection signals only. They cite no standard. Report findings against the element IDs listed (defined in
`../standards/`). SPS elements apply only when Spring Security is a dependency. Spring Boot
`server.servlet.session.cookie.*` defaults are not localized: report only explicit insecure values.

| Signal (API, setting or pattern) | Look in | Indicates | Element(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `authorizeHttpRequests` without a final `anyRequest()` rule, or `anyRequest().permitAll()`; legacy `authorizeRequests`/`WebSecurityConfigurerAdapter` with the same gaps | `SecurityFilterChain` beans, security config classes | No deny-by-default | SPS-01, ATZ-02 |
| `WebSecurityCustomizer` / `web.ignoring()` for paths | security config | Paths outside the filter chain | SPS-02 |
| `@PreAuthorize`/`@PostAuthorize` without `@EnableMethodSecurity` (or legacy `@EnableGlobalMethodSecurity(prePostEnabled = true)`); `@Secured` without `securedEnabled = true`; `@RolesAllowed` without `jsr250Enabled = true` | config classes, services | Method security inert | SPS-03 |
| Repository `findById(id)` returned from a controller without owner/tenant check, `@PostAuthorize` or `#id` expression | controllers, services | IDOR | SPS-04, ATZ-04 |
| `csrf(c -> c.disable())` / `.csrf().disable()` with form login or session cookies | security config | Missing CSRF defense | SPS-08, SES-07 |
| `sessionFixation(f -> f.none())` / `.sessionFixation().none()` | security config | Session fixation | SPS-06, SES-11 |
| Custom servlet login that sets session attributes without `request.changeSessionId()` | login controllers/filters | No session ID renewal | SES-11 |
| GET logout handler; `invalidateHttpSession(false)`; logout that only clears cookies | security config, controllers | Incomplete logout | SPS-07, SES-15 |
| `NoOpPasswordEncoder`, `{noop}` prefixes, `User.withDefaultPasswordEncoder()`, `StandardPasswordEncoder`, `Md5PasswordEncoder`, `MessageDigest` on passwords | config, user services, seed data | Weak password storage | SPS-09, PWS-01 |
| `new BCryptPasswordEncoder(n)` with `n < 10`; `Pbkdf2PasswordEncoder` with low iterations | config | Weak work factor | PWS-04, PWS-05 |
| Registration/change-password flow without `CompromisedPasswordChecker` | account services | No breached-password check | SPS-10 |
| `spring.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.*` with no `audiences` and no `AudienceValidator` | `application*.yml`/`.properties`, decoder beans | `aud` not validated | SPS-11, JWT-05 |
| `NimbusJwtDecoder` with `setJwtValidator(...)` that replaces the defaults; broad `jws-algorithms`; shared `SecretKey` across services | decoder beans | Weakened JWT validation | SPS-12, JWT-02 |
| jjwt `Jwts.parser()` without `verifyWith`/`setSigningKey`; `parseUnsecuredClaims`; auth0 `JWT.decode(...)` used as verification | token services, filters | Signature not verified | JWT-01 |
| `requireProofKey(false)` on a client registration; `authorization-grant-type: password` or implicit | OAuth2 client config | Weak OAuth flow | SPS-13, OAU-04, OAU-06 |
| `http://` `issuer-uri`, `jwk-set-uri` or `redirect-uri` | `application*.yml`/`.properties` | Tokens over plain HTTP | OAU-11 |

## File: `references/standards/spring-security.md`

*Load rule: SPS-01…13. Load when language `java` is detected.*

### Spring Security identity guidance — localized summary

- Applies when `spring-security-*`, `spring-boot-starter-security` or `spring-boot-starter-oauth2-*` is a dependency.
  Spring Boot `server.servlet.session.cookie.*` defaults are **not** localized (gap note per `SKILL.md`).
- Framework elements apply only when that framework is in use; otherwise they don't apply.
- Level: a framework element takes the level of the OWASP element it implements (e.g. a cookie-flag setting implements
  SES-04/SES-05), or `SHOULD` when the vendor only recommends. Severity rules are in `../../SKILL.md`.
- Defaults stated here are the only framework defaults a worker may rely on. Never use remembered defaults.

| ID | Level | Requirement (summary) | Code/config evidence | Check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SPS-01 | MUST | `authorizeHttpRequests` ends with a catch-all (`anyRequest().denyAll()` or `.authenticated()`) so rules form an allow list ("denying by default is a healthy security practice"). | no `anyRequest()` rule; `anyRequest().permitAll()` | SEC-IA-01 |
| SPS-02 | SHOULD | Use `permitAll()` for public/static resources instead of `web.ignoring()` (which drops them from the filter chain). | `WebSecurityCustomizer` ignoring paths | SEC-IA-01 |
| SPS-03 | MUST | Method security annotations are enforced only once enabled: `@PreAuthorize`/`@PostAuthorize` need `@EnableMethodSecurity`; `@Secured` also needs `securedEnabled = true`, `@RolesAllowed` needs `jsr250Enabled = true`. | annotations without `@EnableMethodSecurity` or the matching attribute | SEC-IA-02 |
| SPS-04 | SHOULD | Fine-grained/object decisions use method security with parameters or return values (`@PreAuthorize("… #id …")`, `@PostAuthorize`, `@AuthorizeReturnObject`). | only coarse URL rules for per-object access | SEC-IA-02 |
| SPS-05 | SHOULD | Prefer granting authorities over complex SpEL expressions for authorization logic. | long inline SpEL with string concatenation | SEC-IA-02 |
| SPS-06 | MUST | Keep session fixation protection (default `changeSessionId`; `newSession`/`migrateSession` allowed); never `sessionFixation().none()`. | `sessionFixation(f -> f.none())` | SEC-IA-05 |
| SPS-07 | SHOULD | Logout via POST with CSRF token; default handlers invalidate the HTTP session and clear the security context; `Clear-Site-Data` can clear client storage. | custom GET logout that skips invalidation; `invalidateHttpSession(false)` | SEC-IA-05 |
| SPS-08 | MUST | CSRF protection is on by default; disable it only for backends that serve no browser traffic, and prefer ignoring specific endpoints over global disable. | `csrf(c -> c.disable())` with form/session login | SEC-IA-05 |
| SPS-09 | MUST | Encode passwords with `DelegatingPasswordEncoder` (`PasswordEncoderFactories`) or an adaptive encoder (bcrypt, Argon2, scrypt, PBKDF2); never `NoOpPasswordEncoder` or `User.withDefaultPasswordEncoder()` in production. | `NoOpPasswordEncoder`, `{noop}`, `withDefaultPasswordEncoder`, `StandardPasswordEncoder`/MD5/SHA encoders | SEC-IA-06 |
| SPS-10 | SHOULD | Check passwords against known compromises (`CompromisedPasswordChecker`, e.g. HaveIBeenPwned) on registration and change. | registration/change without compromised check | SEC-IA-10 |
| SPS-11 | MUST | Resource server: `issuer-uri`/`jwk-set-uri` configured (validates signature, `iss`, `exp`, `nbf` by default); `audiences` configured, because `aud` isn't validated otherwise. | no `audiences` property or `AudienceValidator` | SEC-IA-03 |
| SPS-12 | SHOULD | Restrict trusted algorithms explicitly (default RS256 only; `jwsAlgorithm(…)`); a single symmetric key only when issuer and audience are the same party. | broad algorithm lists; shared `SecretKey` across services | SEC-IA-03 |
| SPS-13 | SHOULD | OAuth2 client/login uses authorization code; PKCE for public clients and, by default, confidential clients (`requireProofKey`); registered redirect URI template. | `requireProofKey(false)` without provider reason; non-code grants for users | SEC-IA-04 |
